title: The Reliance Communications – Bank of Baroda Fraud
dek: Four years after the Supreme Court found Anil Ambani in contempt over unpaid Ericsson dues, the CBI opened a fresh case alleging his telecom company defrauded a public sector bank of over ₹2,200 crore.

heroStat.label: wrongful loss alleged to Bank of Baroda

promise.quote: Credit facilities extended to Reliance Communications will be used for their disclosed purpose and repaid according to sanctioned terms.
promise.madeBy: Reliance Communications Ltd., under chairman Anil Ambani
promise.role: Telecom company; borrower from a public sector bank
promise.context: This is a separate CBI case from the company's earlier, already-covered Supreme Court contempt proceedings over unpaid dues to Ericsson — this one concerns an alleged fraud against Bank of Baroda specifically.

target.description: Credit facilities used for their disclosed telecom-business purpose and repaid or restructured transparently, without cheating the lending bank.
target.standard: Standard bank lending covenants and RBI fraud-classification norms.

reality.description: The CBI registered a fresh case against Anil Ambani and Reliance Communications in February 2026, alleging the company cheated Bank of Baroda and caused a wrongful loss of more than ₹2,220 crore. This is distinct from, though part of the same broader pattern as, the company's earlier Supreme Court contempt case over Ericsson dues and its promoter's separate Yes Bank-linked chargesheet, both of which are covered elsewhere on this site.
